kit_requests: A camera hint in place of the guide workaround, for example K.frame(root, {x, y, w, h}, from, to) or camera.hold, so a scene can declare a section's composition explicitly instead of using unpainted boxes with transparent borders.

camera.js measures element boxes, not text extents. A block text box laid out 1520 px wide makes a short title count as full width, and the camera will not centre it. Either measure text nodes with Range.getClientRects or say in AUTHORING that framed text boxes should be shrink-wrapped (w = null).

Allow K.focus in data-cam='drift' scenes, or document that it needs 'frame'. Today path() returns null outside 'frame', so a scene that manages its own view has to use frame mode plus a full-stage guide to get one push-in.

Add a K.unlit or settle companion to K.lit that returns the text colour and keeps or fades the rule. It should also force the lit element to hug its text (inline or align-self:flex-start); otherwise a lit flex or block item underlines its whole box width.

K.focus crop check: warn at boot when visible painted content falls partly outside the focused frame, or offer {fit: 'contain'} that caps the zoom so everything visible stays in frame. Several possible push-ins, such as the network data node and the 11 September row, had to be dropped by hand for this reason.
A crossfade helper for adjacent scenes, so a chapter change does not pass through 0.3–0.5 s of blank paper.
